content.comment_body: Hello, I am encountering an issue when loading a program into [product_name] [article_no]. [product_name] software provides the following error: "The MB memory location is full. The block location has been saved." How can I resolve this? Best regards, [user_name]
Reset your [product_name] by deleting the current program. Go to Program > Edit Program > Delete Program.

Hello, I'm facing the same issue: "La memoria del MB está llena. Se ha guardado la ubicación del bloque." I've already deleted the program from [product_name], but when I try transferring it again from PC to [product_name] I still get the warning. Did you find any solution? Regards, [user_name]

This is not an error but an alert. The internal memory in [product_name] dedicated to storing the locations of function blocks and signals can't accommodate all the information with large programs. You can continue to add functions and signals, but if you upload from [product_name], the arrangement of blocks and signals may become disorganized. However, program execution in [product_name] is unaffected.
Thanks for your helpful explanation. I'm working on a large program (around 300 blocks) and can proceed now. Thank you, [user_name]
Thanks for your response. I have the same issue, but I did not fully understand your explanation. Could you clarify again? Thank you.

Welcome to the forum. Please note that the official language here is English. Kindly write your future posts in English so everyone can participate; if needed, use online translators. The message about layout memory is just a warning, not an error. You can easily transfer programs from PC to [product_name], and the message doesn't impact execution. Keep in mind, when transferring the program back from [product_name] to the PC, the arrangement of blocks may no longer match the original, making the diagram harder to read.

I receive the same message, "The location of MB memory is full. Has kept the location of the block," when saving as a .bin file. After saving, the file is created, but copying it to an SD card to transfer to [product_name] results in the SD card clearing the current program and [product_name] displaying "empty program." There is no program in the SD card or in [product_name]. Is it possible to retain the [product_name] program, or empty/change the MB memory? Thanks and best regards, [user_name]

You can transfer the program to [product_name] and then save it to an SD card if one is inserted into [product_name]. Alternatively, use the menu in [product_name] to save the program from memory to the SD card manually.

Thank you for your answer. So, if a backup .bin file displays the warning "The location of MB memory is full. The block location has been saved," it's not possible to use this .bin file on the SD card to restore the program to [product_name]. In this case, I can only transfer the .lsc program from the PC? Thanks and best regards, [user_name]
Directly storing an .lsc program onto an SD card will not allow [product_name] to run it. Only a .bin program on the SD card can be executed by [product_name].

analysis.insight_summary: Users frequently encounter a warning indicating MB (memory block) capacity is reached when working with large projects on [product_name] using [product_name] software. This warning signals a limitation in storing visual block arrangements, not a functional error. As a result, the visual organization of logic blocks may be lost when uploading programs from [product_name] back to PC, and using SD cards and .bin backups presents challenges for restoring programs without data loss.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect consistent and reliable transfer and backup of programs between PC, [product_name], and SD card, including retention of block locations and prevention of unusable backups or data loss.
